PCE Inflation and Crypto: The Fed's Favorite Number

Guides · 6 min read · Updated June 2026

Ask a crypto trader which inflation report matters and they'll say CPI. Ask the Federal Reserve and the answer is PCE — the gauge it actually targets. If you only watch CPI, you're missing the number the people who set rates care about most.

PCE vs CPI

Both measure inflation, but PCE (Personal Consumption Expenditures) uses a broader, shifting basket of what people actually buy, and it's the metric the Fed officially steers by. It usually runs slightly below CPI. The version to watch is core PCE — stripping out volatile food and energy — because that's what the Fed leans on when deciding policy. We break down CPI itself in the CPI week playbook; PCE is its more authoritative cousin.

Why it can move crypto after CPI already did

PCE lands later in the month, so it acts as a tie-breaker. A cool CPI that had traders pricing rate cuts can be undone by a hot PCE — and since Bitcoin trades rate expectations, it reprices on the surprise. Don't assume the inflation story is settled just because CPI already printed.

Trading it like any release

The discipline is identical to CPI and NFP: know the exact time from the calendar, size so a fast wick can't liquidate you with the position size calculator, skip market orders in the chaotic first minute, and read funding afterward to separate a real move from a stop-hunt.
